### foundation-core__CORE_ENGINE_FORMAL_MODEL.md
   1: # CORE_ENGINE_FORMAL_MODEL.md — Core Engine Formal Model Story (Consolidated)
   2: 
   3: ## 1. Purpose and Status
   4: This document is the consolidated story-so-far for DNA Calc core engine formal/semantic modeling.
   5: 
   6: It is not:
   7: - the pathfinder functional-scope source (that remains in DnaVisiCalc docs),
   8: - the final formal model design,
   9: - the final theorem/spec artifact set.
  10: 
  11: It is:
  12: - the single active funnel for core-engine formal ideas,
  13: - a triaged and tagged consolidation of what we currently know, suspect, and need to decide,
  14: - the working base for iterative review and promotion into stable formal semantics over time.
  15: 
  16: ## 2. Source Corpus and Context
  17: Core context docs used in this consolidation:
  18: - `README.md`
  19: - `CHARTER.md`
  20: - `ARCHITECTURE_AND_REQUIREMENTS.md`
  21: - `OPERATIONS.md`
  22: - `notes/BRAINSTORM_NOTES.md`
  23: 
  24: Archived formal-idea sources consolidated here:
  25: - `notes/archive/formal-model/FORMAL_MODELS_IDEAS.md`
  26: - `notes/archive/formal-model/FORMAL_MODEL_REMAINING_NOTES.md`
  27: - `notes/archive/formal-model/FORMAL_CORE_STATUS_AND_SUGGESTIONS_DRAFT.md`
  28: 
  29: ## 3. Triage Tags and Promotion Rules
  30: This document uses explicit tags on ideas and decisions:
  31: - `Baseline`: intended current core model baseline.
  32: - `Provisional`: accepted direction with unresolved semantics.
  33: - `Exploratory`: research/design-space material not yet normative.
  34: - `Deferred`: explicit backlog item retained for later formalization.
  35: - `Out-of-core`: important system concern, but not part of the core-engine formal model.
  36: 
  37: Promotion from `Exploratory`/`Provisional` to `Baseline` requires:
  38: - a concrete semantic decision need (profile/pack/replay impact),
  39: - deterministic artifact/test expression,
  40: - doctrine consistency,
  41: - synthesis decision logging.
  42: 
  43: ## 4. Core Boundary for This Document
  44: Core engine scope captured here includes:
  45: - protocol-facing core semantics (`dispatch/query/subscribe/capability` behavior shape),
  46: - profile and compatibility semantics as they constrain core behavior,
  47: - epoch/status model and calc-delta model,
  48: - dependency/recalc semantics (including cycles/iteration),
  49: - operation transition/replay semantics,
  50: - structural rewrite and reference model semantics,
  51: - core entities participating in dependency semantics (cells, names, charts, controls as modeled source/sink nodes).
  52: 
  53: `Out-of-core` system areas are tracked only as interface/seam constraints:
  54: - VBA runtime hosting/editor,
  55: - full file adapters and OOXML lowering,
  56: - UI rendering architecture,
  57: - collaboration envelope implementation details.
  58: 
  59: ## 5. Consolidated Core Semantics Baseline
  60: 
  61: ### 5.1 Protocol Surface and Contracts (`Baseline`)
  62: Protocol surface (identical across implementations):
  63: - dispatch ops/transactions,
  64: - query snapshots/state,
  65: - subscribe to deltas/events,
  66: - capability negotiation.
  67: 
  68: Contract requirements:
  69: - versioned protocol surface,
  70: - schema-defined payloads,
  71: - deterministic replay-compatible semantics.
  72: 
  73: ### 5.2 Profiles, Gates, and Compatibility (`Baseline`)
  74: Profiles are semantic control planes for core behavior:
  75: - bind behavior to `profile_id` + `profile_version`,
  76: - define semantics and structural-edit rules,
  77: - define required obligation packs,
  78: - define degradation classes (`Native` / `Lowered` / `Opaque` / `Rejected`),
  79: - define feature-gate tokens (for example stream semantics and external update policies).
  80: 
  81: ### 5.3 Epoch and CalcDelta Semantics (`Baseline`)
  82: Epoch model:
  83: - `committed_epoch`: latest accepted changes,
  84: - `stabilized_epoch`: latest epoch with stabilized derived outputs,
  85: - `value_epoch`: per-derived-value epoch stamp.
  86: 
  87: Status/invariant model:
  88: - explicit stale/pending/ready/error visibility,
  89: - no stale commit (`value must match claimed input epoch`),
  90: - structural commit exclusivity,
  91: - pinned-epoch-safe GC behavior.
  92: 
  93: CalcDelta model (derived output, not mutation log):
  94: ```text
  95: ChangeEntryKind =
  96:   | CellValue
  97:   | NameValue
  98:   | ChartOutput
  99:   | SpillRegion
 100:   | CellFormat
 101: ```
 102: Required properties:
 103: - epoch tagging,
 104: - deterministic emission policy,
 105: - drain-style retrieval contract accepted as baseline.
 106: 
 107: ### 5.4 Calculation Semantics (`Baseline`)
 108: Pipeline semantics:
 109: - parse -> bind -> dependency graph -> invalidation closure -> schedule -> evaluate -> commit.
 110: 
 111: Identity model for evaluation graph:
 112: ```text
 113: NodeId =
 114:   | Cell(CellId)
 115:   | Name(NameId)
 116:   | Chart(ChartId)
 117: ```
 118: 
 119: Incrementality:
 120: - invariant-oriented model (`necessary`, `stale`, `height`, `scope`) retained,
 121: - baseline dirty-closure model retained:
 122:   - `dirty_nodes`,
 123:   - `reverse_deps`,
 124:   - deterministic dirty-subgraph evaluation.
 125: 
 126: Determinism requirements:
 127: - stable scheduling behavior,
 128: - explicit numeric reduction policy where relevant,
 129: - persisted calc order artifacts treated as cache/diagnostic, not semantic truth.
 130: 
 131: ### 5.5 External Invalidation and UDF Semantics (`Baseline` + `Provisional`)
 132: Three invalidation classes:
 133: - `Standard`: upstream-dependent invalidation,
 134: - `Volatile`: host-cycle invalidation,
 135: - `ExternallyInvalidated`: explicit external signal invalidation.
 136: 
 137: External stream/update semantics retained:
 138: - explicit external-update operation representation (`OpExternalUpdate`-style semantics),
 139: - explicit topic identity and sequence handling,
 140: - deterministic ordering/dedupe/coalescing policy by profile,
 141: - replay-bundle expectations for conformance/minimization flows.
 142: 
 143: Required split:
 144: - volatile invalidation path and external invalidation path are distinct,
 145: - both converge through deterministic dirty-closure/evaluation pipeline.
 146: 
 147: UDF baseline:
 148: - registration/unregistration,
 149: - volatility-class declaration,
 150: - externally driven invalidation hooks,
 151: - caller-driven deterministic execution contract.
 152: 
 153: `Provisional`/open:
 154: - deeper pure/impure function-class formal treatment for dependency-discovery interaction.
 155: 
 156: ### 5.6 Controls and Charts as Core Entities (`Baseline`)
 157: Controls/charts are core engine entities (not UI-only state):
 158: - controls as named-value source entities with metadata/constraints,
 159: - charts as sink entities producing structured outputs,
 160: - both participate in dependency semantics and dirty propagation,
 161: - lifecycle changes flow through explicit operation kinds and replay artifacts.
 162: 
 163: ## 6. Core Formal State Kernel and Transition Semantics
 164: 
 165: ### 6.1 Tree-Grid Hybrid Kernel (`Baseline`)
 166: Persistent model shape:
 167: - immutable green core,
 168: - ephemeral red context facades,
 169: - ID-based identity (`RowId`/`ColId`/`CellId`), coordinate projection derived.
 170: 
 171: Canonical identity sketch:
 172: ```text
 173: type Epoch = u64
 174: type WorkbookId = opaque
 175: type SheetId = opaque
 176: type RowId = opaque
 177: type ColId = opaque
 178: type CellId = RowId * ColId
 179: ```
 180: 
 181: Tree-grid hybrid concept retained from earlier notes:
 182: - workbook/sheet/grid structural substrate,
 183: - no arbitrary unrooted calc-node bags,
 184: - augmentation structures may attach and participate via defined seams.
 185: 
 186: ### 6.2 Layered Formal Model (`Baseline`)
 187: ```text
 188: Layer S: Structure
 189: Layer R: References
 190: Layer D: Dependencies
 191: Layer V: Values/iteration state

### foundation-core__OPERATIONS.md
   1: # OPERATIONS.md — DNA Calc Operations
   2: 
   3: ## 1. Purpose
   4: Operations defines how DNA Calc is developed, stabilized, and evolved under the Mission and Doctrine. It is designed to withstand “agentic coding weather” and frequent plan changes.
   5: 
   6: ## 2. Structure (Green/Red/Blue) and Veto
   7: ### 2.1 Responsibilities
   8: **Green (Spec & Assurance)**
   9: - Owns DSL specs, proofs, protocol specs, OCaml oracle, cases, conformance packs.
  10: - Owns profile definitions, profile versioning rules, and negotiation schemas.
  11: - Owns `CORE_ENGINE_FORMAL_MODEL.md` as the detailed formal-semantics working document.
  12: - Curates minimized regressions and “known quirks” documentation.
  13: - **Has veto on declaring a profile “stabilized/green.”**
  14: 
  15: **Red (Rust engine)**
  16: - Implements the protocol surface and passes Green’s packs.
  17: - Focuses on hard-rock correctness under concurrency and performance scaling.
  18: 
  19: **Blue (.NET engine)**
  20: - Implements the identical protocol surface and passes Green’s packs.
  21: - Provides independent confirmation of spec clarity and implementation feasibility.
  22: 
  23: **Logistics (Tooling & Coordination)**
  24: - Builds and maintains `meta` orchestration, CI wiring, artifact storage/reporting, dashboards.
  25: - Keeps cycle time low and reproducibility high.
  26: - Generally .NET-first tooling, with small Rust utilities when warranted.
  27: 
  28: ### 2.2 Module Triads
  29: Every major spec/module area is managed by a **triad**:
  30: - **Design** representative (spec intent and structure),
  31: - **Assurance** representative (packs, proofs, test strategy),
  32: - **Delivery** representative (Red/Blue implementation implications).
  33: 
  34: Triads resolve ambiguity early and ensure artifacts remain consistent.
  35: 
  36: ## 3. Development Recalc Cycle (mirrors calculation)
  37: The project evolves through a “recalc” cycle operating on DAGs.
  38: 
  39: ### 3.1 DAGs
  40: - **Spec DAG**: Lean modules, TLA+ modules, schemas/IDL, profiles.
  41: - **Assurance DAG**: obligation packs, oracle runs, minimized cases, perf signatures.
  42: - **Implementation DAG**: Red modules, Blue modules, adapters, protocol surfaces.
  43: - **Interop DAG** (later/heavier): Excel differential packs, file adapter conformance.
  44: 
  45: ### 3.2 Phase Model
  46: 1. **Edit / Dirty Marking**
  47:    - Any change marks a set of nodes dirty (modules, packs, profiles, protocols), including `OpExternalUpdate`.
  48: 2. **Dependency Closure**
  49:    - `meta` computes impacted obligations and required version bumps.
  50: 3. **Scheduling**
  51:    - Work is dispatched along parallel tracks: Design / Assurance / Delivery / Logistics.
  52: 4. **Execution**
  53:    - Proofs/model checks, oracle runs, engine conformance, perf signatures.
  54:    - For behavior-sensitive changes, execute a coupled evidence lane: semantics/spec delta, proof/model output, deterministic replay artifacts, and scaling signature evidence.
  55: 5. **Stabilization**
  56:    - A profile is stabilized when its required obligation packs pass and artifacts are emitted.
  57: 6. **Meta-epoch Commit**
  58:    - Publish capability manifest + conformance report + regression updates.
  59: 
  60: ### 3.3 Sequence-Only Planning Doctrine (No Time Schedules)
  61: Project execution planning is sequence-based, not calendar-based.
  62: 
  63: Mandatory rule:
  64: 1. Plans and execution notes must not use date-based or duration-based commitments (for example deadlines, ETA dates, week-based schedules, or "finish by X time").
  65: 2. Execution order must be expressed using:
  66:    - priority,
  67:    - dependency/`depends_on` relations,
  68:    - blocker status,
  69:    - gate/pack readiness criteria,
  70:    - risk and impact ordering.
  71: 3. Progress is reported by state transitions and obligation closure (for example `planned -> in_progress -> blocked -> complete`), not by elapsed time targets.
  72: 4. If temporal metadata is captured for audit/provenance (timestamps in artifacts), it is observational only and must not be used as a planning commitment axis.
  73: 
  74: ### 3.4 Auto vs Manual Modes (dev analogy)
  75: - **Auto**: CI runs the full required packs for affected profiles.
  76: - **Manual**: local development may defer heavy packs, but merge requires stabilization.

### foundation-core__CHARTER.md
   1: # CHARTER.md — DNA Calc Charter
   2: 
   3: ## 1. Mission
   4: **DNA Calc Mission**  
   5: DNA Calc is a near-formal, state-of-the-art spreadsheet platform that matches Excel’s behavior with high fidelity while remaining rigorously specified, verifiable, and built to evolve. It is a clean-room implementation based only on public documentation, published research, and reproducible observation of Excel’s behavior—never proprietary sources or reverse-engineering of internals. DNA Calc prioritizes correctness under concurrency, graceful degradation across versions and profiles, and stable, versioned interfaces that support a long-lived ecosystem of tools, add-ins, and automation.
   6: 
   7: ## 2. Doctrine
   8: Doctrine is mandatory operating guidance. **Hygiene** is listed before **Evolution**.
   9: 
  10: ### 2.1 Hygiene Doctrine
  11: 1. **Spec-first (or spec-with) changes**  
  12:    Behavior changes are not “done” until spec + cases are updated and gates pass.
  13: 2. **Computed obligations, no hand-waving**  
  14:    Required checks are determined mechanically from diffs and profiles; bypass is rare and explicit.
  15: 3. **One-command readiness**  
  16:    `meta check` (or equivalent) is the standard way to declare a state “green.”
  17: 4. **Regressions are assets**  
  18:    Every bug becomes a minimized, machine-replayable trace/case artifact and remains in the corpus.
  19: 5. **Determinism-first debugging**  
  20:    Deterministic modes exist for triage and conformance runs; non-determinism is opt-in and labeled.
  21: 6. **Evidence discipline**  
  22:    Every Excel-compatibility claim is backed by public sources and/or a reproducible observation harness.
  23: 7. **Coupled assurance stack**  
  24:    Claims of correctness must stay coupled across semantics, proofs/models, executable tests, and CI gate artifacts.
  25: 
  26: ### 2.2 Evolution Doctrine
  27: 1. **Profiles are the semantics spine**  
  28:    Documents bind to `profile_id` + `profile_version`. Breaking semantic changes require profile bumps.
  29: 2. **Protocols are versioned and negotiated**  
  30:    OpLog, engine protocol surface, automation protocol, UI protocol—each has explicit versions and negotiation.
  31: 3. **Degrade gracefully; never crash**  
  32:    Unsupported or unknown features must preserve data (opaque) and/or surface explicit deterministic errors/warnings.
  33: 4. **Unknown parts round-trip**  
  34:    When feasible, unrecognized file parts and extension payloads are preserved byte-for-byte.
  35: 5. **Migrations are explicit and replayable**  
  36:    Migrations are expressed as operations and are testable/replayable.
  37: 6. **No hidden mutation pathways**  
  38:    All persistent state changes flow through the operation model; no “special cases” for UI, scripts, VBA, XLL, or collaboration.
  39: 
  40: ### 2.3 Named Program Principles
  41: 1. **Alien Artifact leverage**
  42:    Use mathematically strong methods when they remove ambiguity and increase confidence, but keep each method tied to executable invariants and artifacts.
  43: 2. **Design for Evolution**
  44:    Keep seams explicit, versioned, and negotiable so behavior can expand without semantic drift or silent breakage.
  45: 
  46: ## 3. Program Structure and Names
  47: ### 3.1 System Family
  48: - **DNA Calc** (code token: `DnaCalc`) — the Goldilocks long-term foundation.
  49: - **DNA VisiCalc** (`DnaVisiCalc`) — Round 0 pathfinder.  
  50:   Functional scope authority for Round 0 is maintained in the DnaVisiCalc docs set (`SPEC_v0.md`, `ENGINE_REQUIREMENTS.md`, `ENGINE_API.md`); Foundation doctrine/process docs must remain consistent with that scope.
  51: - **DNA PreCalc** (`DnaPreCalc`) — Round 1 full end-to-end.
  52: - **DNA SuperCalc** (`DnaSuperCalc`) — Round 2 refactor/perfection pass.
  53: - **DNA Calc** (`DnaCalc`) — Round 3 synthesized long-term product.
  54: 
  55: ### 3.2 Team Colors
  56: - **Green** — Spec stack + verification: DSLs, Lean proofs, TLA+ models, OCaml oracle, conformance packs.
  57: - **Red** — Rust implementation.
  58: - **Blue** — .NET implementation.
  59: 
  60: (“Logistics” exists as a function; it may be implemented primarily in .NET tooling.)
  61: 
  62: ## 4. Clean-room Rule (Non-negotiable)
  63: DNA Calc development relies only on:
  64: - public specifications and documentation,
  65: - published research,
  66: - reproducible observation of Excel behavior.
  67: 
  68: Excluded:
  69: - proprietary code, restricted materials, decompilation/disassembly of Excel internals, or reverse engineering of internals.
  70: 
  71: ## 5. Glossary (short)
  72: - **Profile**: A versioned semantics bundle defining meaning, compatibility rules, and required obligation packs.
  73: - **OpLog**: The operation log—the single representation of persistent state changes.
  74: - **Epoch / Meta-epoch**: Epoch versions document state; meta-epochs version stabilized project states (profiles + packs + implementations).
  75: - **Calc stabilized**: A runtime/data state where derived outputs are complete for a declared scope and epoch.
  76: - **Profile green**: A release/readiness state where all required obligation packs for a profile are passing.
  77: - **Stabilized epoch**: The latest epoch whose derived values are complete for a declared scope.
  78: - **Meta-epoch commit**: A published stabilization checkpoint containing capability manifest, conformance report, and regression updates.
  79: - **Artifact freeze**: A required set of versioned artifacts that must be locked before advancing rounds or declaring a profile green.
  80: - **External update op**: An explicit OpLog operation representing inbound STREAM/RTD-like value changes.
  81: - **Stream semantics version**: A profile-scoped version token controlling STREAM/external update behavior.
  82: - **Stream replay bundle**: A versioned artifact containing topic declarations and ordered update envelopes for deterministic replay.
  83: - **Degradation class**: Policy outcome for unsupported behavior (`Native`, `Lowered`, `Opaque`, `Rejected`).
  84: - **Obligation pack**: A computed set of checks required to claim readiness for a profile.
  85: - **Capability manifest**: Runtime/Build metadata describing supported protocols, profiles, features, and pack results.
### foundation-core__ARCHITECTURE_AND_REQUIREMENTS.md
   1: # ARCHITECTURE_AND_REQUIREMENTS.md — DNA Calc Architecture and Requirements
   2: 
   3: ## 1. Overview
   4: DNA Calc is a near-formal spreadsheet system with two independent engines (Rust and .NET) sharing identical protocol surfaces and validated against a Green-owned spec stack: Lean (semantics proofs), TLA+ (concurrency protocol checks), OCaml oracle (executable reference), and conformance packs.
   5: 
   6: ### 1.1 Three Hard Boundaries (core architectural shape)
   7: 1. **OpLog (Operations)**
   8:    - All persistent state changes are operations (including structural edits, external updates, macro edits).
   9: 2. **DocSnapshot (Versioned Document State)**
  10:    - Immutable snapshots per epoch/meta-epoch. Inputs are truth; derived values are caches.
  11: 3. **CalcDeltas (Derived Outputs)**
  12:    - Engine produces deltas tagged with version info (epoch/value_epoch) and explicit stale/pending status.
  13: 
  14: ## 2. Requirements Taxonomy (how to write requirements)
  15: ### 2.1 Architecture-independent requirements (REQ-)
  16: Observable behaviors and quality targets, independent of internal mechanisms.
  17: 
  18: ### 2.2 Architecture-dependent constraints (CONSTR-)
  19: Enforceable structural rules derived from Mission/Doctrine.
  20: 
  21: ### 2.3 Architecture-anchored intents and realizations (INT-/REAL-)
  22: - **Intent (INT-)**: desired outcome, mechanism-agnostic.
  23: - **Realization (REAL-)**: precise, testable specification anchored to chosen architecture.
  24: 
  25: ## 3. System Architecture (A1)
  26: This section now includes a formal-core layer model intended to be shared by Green proofs/models, the OCaml oracle, and both delivery engines.
  27: Detailed core formal/semantic model development is maintained in `CORE_ENGINE_FORMAL_MODEL.md`.
  28: This document should keep architecture-level summaries and stable constraints, with minimal duplication of formal-core detail.
  29: 
  30: ### 3.1 Protocol Surface (identical across Red/Blue)
  31: - Dispatch ops/transactions.
  32: - Query snapshots/state.
  33: - Subscribe to deltas/events.
  34: - Capability negotiation.
  35: 
  36: Detailed core semantics are in `CORE_ENGINE_FORMAL_MODEL.md`:
  37: - protocol baseline: Section `5.1`,
  38: - operation/replay semantics: Section `6.4`.
  39: 
  40: ### 3.2 Profiles, Feature Gates, and Compatibility
  41: - Profiles remain the semantic spine (`profile_id` + `profile_version`) for compatibility, feature gates, obligation packs, and degrade behavior.
  42: 
  43: Detailed core profile semantics are in `CORE_ENGINE_FORMAL_MODEL.md` Section `5.2`.
  44: 
  45: ### 3.3 Epoch Model (MVCC-style)
  46: - Core epoch semantics (`committed/stabilized/value epoch`, stale/pending visibility, pinning/GC constraints) remain mandatory.
  47: - Core calc-delta derived-output semantics remain mandatory.
  48: 
  49: Detailed definitions are in `CORE_ENGINE_FORMAL_MODEL.md` Section `5.3`.
  50: 
  51: ### 3.4 Calculation Engine Pipeline (conceptual)
  52: - Core pipeline remains parse/bind/dependency/invalidation/schedule/evaluate/commit with deterministic and incremental requirements.
  53: - `NodeId`-based dependency identity remains baseline.
  54: - Both invariant-oriented and dirty-closure propagation models remain valid formal baselines.
  55: 
  56: Detailed definitions are in `CORE_ENGINE_FORMAL_MODEL.md` Section `5.4`.
  57: 
  58: ### 3.5 External Streaming and RTD-like Behavior
  59: - Pathfinder: `STREAM("topic")` is acceptable and deterministic (epoch-scoped external provider).
  60: - Full system: RTD support (topic lifecycle, updates, invalidations) is a core interop feature.
  61: - External updates must appear as explicit `OpExternalUpdate` ops (`topic_id`, `topic_seq`, payload ref/envelope) and be replayable for test harnesses where required.
  62: - STREAM/external update semantics include explicit topic identity, dedupe rules, ordering guarantees, and coalescing policy.
  63: - Profile policy defines whether oracle values are local-only or shared for collaboration scenarios.
  64: - A stream replay bundle (topic declarations, updates, timing/order envelope) is a required artifact for conformance and minimization.
  65: 
  66: #### 3.5.1 External Invalidation vs Volatile Invalidation
  67: - External functions (`STREAM`, RTD, and profile-marked externally-invalidated UDFs) recalculate on explicit external signal, not on every volatile cycle.
  68: - Volatile functions recalculate on invalidation cycles triggered by host policy.
  69: - Distinct invalidation pathways are required:
  70:   - volatile invalidation scope (global or class-based),
  71:   - external invalidation scope (targeted by provider/topic/UDF identity).
  72: - Both pathways converge on the same dirty-closure propagation and deterministic evaluation pipeline.
  73: 
  74: ### 3.6 External UDFs / XLL-like integration
  75: Pathfinder scope includes:
  76: - external UDF registration/unregistration with explicit volatility class,
  77: - externally driven invalidation hooks (`invalidate_udf`) that feed normal dirty-closure propagation,
  78: - deterministic caller-driven execution (no autonomous internal timers/threads in pathfinder engine boundary),
  79: - UDFs treated as pure-oracle from Lean/TLA+ perspective (semantics parameterized by oracle results).
  80: 
  81: Volatility classification:
  82: - `Standard`: recalculates when upstream dependencies change.
  83: - `Volatile`: recalculates on host invalidation cycle.
  84: - `ExternallyInvalidated`: recalculates on explicit external signal.
  85: 
  86: Built-in and UDF volatility classification is profile-governed and must be reflected in capability/profile artifacts.
  87: 
  88: Full system adds:
  89: - full XLL compatibility including marshalling/lifetime contracts and RTD integration.
  90: - XLL is in-process with the engine; boundary contracts are formally specified and validated by Green packs.
  91: 
  92: ### 3.6.1 Controls and Charts as Engine Entities
  93: - Controls/charts are core engine entities participating in dependency semantics and operation/replay lifecycle.
  94: 
  95: Detailed core semantics are in `CORE_ENGINE_FORMAL_MODEL.md` Section `5.6`.
  96: 
  97: ### 3.7 VBA and Macros (outside core)
  98: - VBA runtime and editor live outside the core engine.
  99: - Core engine stores the VBA project as a document object:
 100:   - opaque blob (e.g., `vbaProject.bin`) + minimal metadata.
 101: - Application layer glues:
 102:   - file I/O ↔ engine (store/retrieve blob),
 103:   - VBA runtime ↔ engine (macros emit ops via protocol),
 104:   - macro execution occurs in an exclusive mutation mode (serialized event stream).

 106: Windows-only COM automation is a separate facade layered on top of the identical protocol surface.

 108: ### 3.8 File I/O (outside core, full fidelity)

 111:   - preserve unknown/unsupported OOXML parts where feasible (opaque attachments),

 117: - Collaboration modeled as replication of the OpLog.

 120: - Derived calc is generally local; external oracles (RTD) may be local or shared depending on profile policy.

 131: - View state is partially document-backed (saved view settings) and partially session state.
 132: - UI reliability requires property-level invariants for geometry/hit-test consistency and deterministic RenderPlan validation.
 133: 
 134: ### 3.10.1 Core and Non-core Interaction Summary
 135: - UI/TUI layers read snapshots/deltas and dispatch explicit operations; no hidden persistent core mutation path is allowed.
 136: - File adapters translate external formats to/from core entities and operations, and surface degradation outcomes explicitly.
 137: - VBA/macro runtimes execute outside core and interact through operation pathways.
 138: - Collaboration adapters replicate operation envelopes and preserve causality/idempotency constraints.

 303: ### 6.4 Deferred Functional Expansion Backlog (Retained From Pathfinder Gap Analysis)

### dag-research-synthesis__05_deep_research_synthesis.md
   1: # Deep Research Synthesis: DAG Computation Theory for Spreadsheet Engines
   2: 
   3: ## Executive synthesis
   4: The strongest foundation for a spreadsheet-style DAG engine is not a single theory but a layered stack:
   5: 1. **Graph-theoretic skeleton** (topological order + SCC decomposition),
   6: 2. **Fixed-point semantics** for stabilization and cycle policy,
   7: 3. **Incremental maintenance discipline** (dirty/stale/necessary + dynamic dependency handling),
   8: 4. **Selective advanced incrementalization** (SAC/delta/differential) where cost justifies complexity.
   9: 
  10: This layered model aligns well with DNA Calc's existing architecture commitments (epochs, deterministic replay, profile-governed behavior) and gives clear proof/pack obligations.
  11: 
  12: ## Core architecture implications
  13: 
  14: ### 1) Separate semantic truth from scheduling mechanics
  15: - Semantic truth: fixed-point or acyclic evaluation result definition.
  16: - Scheduling mechanics: concrete algorithm (full rebuild, dynamic-topo, trace repair).
  17: 
  18: Why:
  19: - Enables swapping runtime algorithms without semantic drift.
  20: - Supports profile-based guarantees and deterministic mode.
  21: 
  22: ### 2) Make invalidation state a formal object
  23: Adopt explicit state model for each node/cell class:
  24: - `clean`, `stale`, `necessary`, `recomputed` (names can vary).
  25: 
  26: Why:
  27: - This is where most "hidden behavior" bugs occur.
  28: - SAC and Incremental literature show this is key to tractable debugging and analyzability.
  29: 
  30: ### 3) Treat dynamic dependencies as first-class
  31: Dynamic references (INDIRECT-like, external lookups) should not be bolted onto static DAG assumptions.
  32: 
  33: Use explicit lanes:
  34: - static dependencies (compile-time discoverable),
  35: - dynamic dependencies (evaluation-time observed, tokenized/provenance tracked).
  36: 
  37: ### 4) Reserve heavy math for high-leverage lanes
  38: Not every part needs full differential/timely machinery.
  39: 
  40: Recommended:
  41: - baseline: graph + invalidation + deterministic scheduling,
  42: - advanced: delta/differential model for external streaming and high-update hotspots.
  43: 
  44: ## Theoretical "best fit" shortlist
  45: 
  46: ### A. Mandatory baseline theories
  47: 1. Topological ordering and SCC decomposition.
  48: 2. Fixed-point reasoning for cycle/iteration semantics.
  49: 3. Deterministic replay and dependency soundness invariants.
  50: 
  51: ### B. High-value extension theories
  52: 1. Self-adjusting computation for dynamic incremental repair.
  53: 2. Dynamic cycle/topo maintenance for edit-heavy workloads.
  54: 3. Incremental lambda-calculus / change-theory for function-level optimization and formal proofs.
  55: 
  56: ### C. Strategic future theories
  57: 1. Timely/Differential model for external update semantics.
  58: 2. Semiring provenance for explainability and algebraic trace reasoning.
  59: 
  60: ## Risks if theory is ignored
  61: 1. Hidden non-determinism in parallel/invalidation handling.
  62: 2. Over-recompute and performance collapse under dynamic references.
  63: 3. Unprovable behavior drift between implementations.
  64: 4. Inability to explain conflicting outputs in conformance investigations.
  65: 
  66: ## Recommended next execution sequence
  67: 1. Formalize minimal DAG state transition model and invariants (clean/stale/necessary/recomputed).
  68: 2. Add explicit conformance requirements for dynamic dependency token lifecycle.
  69: 3. Build empirical comparison pack: full rebuild vs dynamic-topo maintenance.
  70: 4. Add targeted SAC-inspired prototype for one dynamic dependency lane.
  71: 5. Reassess whether differential/timely model is required for external-stream-heavy profiles.
  72: 
  73: ## Quality notes
  74: - Source set is strong on primary papers/specs and implementation references.
  75: - Some transfer conclusions are synthesis-level (inferred), not direct theorem statements.
  76: - Best immediate value is to convert this into explicit requirement/proof-pack rows, not to over-generalize architecture prematurely.

### dnavisicalc-spec__SPEC_v0.md
   1: # DNA VisiCalc Core Engine Spec v0
   2: 
   3: ## 1. Purpose
   4: This document defines the current Round-0 core engine compatibility scope.
   5: 
   6: It is the top-priority repo-local specification for engine behavior.
   7: 
   8: Repository integration scope (file adapter/TUI/repo crate boundaries) is maintained in `docs/SPEC_v0_INTEGRATION_APPENDIX.md`.
   9: 
  10: ## 2. Core Engine Scope
  11: The engine contract is implementation-independent and covers:
  12: - deterministic, in-memory spreadsheet behavior,
  13: - host-driven mutation and recalculation APIs,
  14: - formula/value semantics,
  15: - structural rewrite semantics,
  16: - volatility/invalidation behavior,
  17: - UDF integration,
  18: - controls/charts/change tracking entities,
  19: - formatting and deterministic bulk enumeration surfaces.
  20: 
  21: ## 3. Normative v0 Engine Requirements
  22: 
  23: ### 3.1 Engine Boundary
  24: - Pure in-memory API.
  25: - Externally-driven execution only (no internal timers/threads/I/O).
  26: - Deterministic behavior for identical inputs and operation sequences.
  27: 
  28: ### 3.2 Sheet and Address Model
  29: - Single worksheet.
  30: - VisiCalc-size bounds by default: `A1..BK254` (63 columns x 254 rows).
  31: - A1 parsing supports:
  32:   - relative refs (`A1`),
  33:   - mixed absolute refs (`$A1`, `A$1`),
  34:   - fully absolute refs (`$A$1`),
  35:   - ranges (`A1:B7`, `A1...B7`).
  36: 
  37: ### 3.3 Cell and Name Inputs
  38: - Cells and names accept numeric, text, formula, and clear operations.
  39: - Names are case-insensitive, normalized uppercase, and validated against identifier/function/cell-ref conflicts.
  40: 
  41: ### 3.4 Formula Surface
  42: - Arithmetic, comparison, concatenation, and logical evaluation.
  43: - Dynamic arrays and spill semantics including spill references (`A1#`).
  44: - Explicit v0 function surface (aligned with current Rust baseline):
  45:   - aggregates: `SUM`, `MIN`, `MAX`, `AVERAGE`, `COUNT`
  46:   - conditional/error handling: `IF`, `IFERROR`, `IFNA`, `NA`, `ERROR`
  47:   - logical predicates: `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, `ISERROR`, `ISNA`, `ISBLANK`, `ISTEXT`, `ISNUMBER`, `ISLOGICAL`, `ERROR.TYPE`
  48:   - core math/scientific: `ABS`, `INT`, `ROUND`, `SIGN`, `SQRT`, `EXP`, `LN`, `LOG10`, `SIN`, `COS`, `TAN`, `ATN`, `PI`
  49:   - financial/lookup: `NPV`, `PV`, `FV`, `PMT`, `LOOKUP`
  50:   - text: `CONCAT`, `LEN`
  51:   - dynamic arrays and lambda family: `SEQUENCE`, `RANDARRAY`, `LET`, `LAMBDA`, `MAP`
  52:   - reference helpers: `INDIRECT`, `OFFSET`, `ROW`, `COLUMN`
  53:   - volatile/stream: `NOW`, `RAND`, `STREAM`
  54: - Stage priority for non-Rust implementations:
  55:   - critical first: `LET`, `LAMBDA`, `MAP`, `INDIRECT`, `OFFSET`, `SEQUENCE`, `RANDARRAY`, `STREAM`
  56:   - lower priority in staged runs: trig/scientific and financial/lookup categories, but still part of the target v0 surface.
  57: - `STREAM` semantics are explicit (not Excel-derived):
  58:   - call shape: `STREAM(period_secs [, LAMBDA(counter)])`,
  59:   - `period_secs` must be a positive number,
  60:   - stream state is per formula cell; return value is that cell's stream counter (starting at `0`),
  61:   - stream counters advance only through host-driven `tick_streams(elapsed_secs)` invalidation,
  62:   - no autonomous/background ticking inside the engine,
  63:   - if lambda is provided, it is applied to the counter and may return scalar or array.
  64: - `LAMBDA`/`MAP` are fully dynamic-array aware:
  65:   - lambda parameters may receive scalar or array values,
  66:   - `MAP` must support array broadcasting across inputs,
  67:   - lambda return values may be arrays and must participate in deterministic spill tiling/broadcast output.
  68: - `INDIRECT` supports both A1 and R1C1 text references.
  69: - `RAND`/`RANDARRAY` outputs remain within bounds and change via small perturbations on explicit recalculation events.
  70: 
  71: ### 3.5 Recalc and Epoch Model
  72: - `committed_epoch`, `stabilized_epoch`, and per-value `value_epoch`.
  73: - `Automatic` and `Manual` recalc modes.
  74: - Internal recalculation strategy is non-normative (dependency graph/tree shape, scheduling, incremental vs full recompute are implementation choices).
  75: - Normative requirement is externally observable behavior: deterministic stabilized outputs and correct epoch/staleness semantics for identical input + API-call sequences.
  76: 
  77: ### 3.6 Structural Rewrite Path (Required)
  78: - Row/column structural mutations are in-scope:
  79:   - `insert_row`, `delete_row`, `insert_col`, `delete_col`.
  80: - Formula/name references are rewritten deterministically.
  81: - Invalidated references are surfaced explicitly (for example `#REF!` behavior).
  82: - Mixed and absolute references must preserve anchoring flags through rewrites; coordinate rewriting under structural edits applies to all reference classes (`A1`, `$A1`, `A$1`, `$A$1`).
  83: - Structural mutation requests use a tri-state outcome model:
  84:   - `Applied`: mutation accepted and committed.
  85:   - `Rejected`: request is valid but cannot be executed due to structural/policy constraints.
  86:   - `Invalid`: request is malformed or out of contract.
  87: - Rejected structural requests are atomic no-ops:
  88:   - no partial mutation,
  89:   - no `committed_epoch` increment,
  90:   - deterministic, user-visible rejection reason.
  91: 
  92: ### 3.7 Iteration and Cycle Handling
  93: - SCC cycle detection remains deterministic.
  94: - Engine supports iterative cycle mode via iteration configuration (`enabled`, max iterations, convergence tolerance).
  95: - When iteration is disabled, circular references follow Excel-style non-iterative behavior:
  96:   - no hard recalculation failure solely due to circularity,
  97:   - circular paths read prior stabilized values when available, otherwise `0.0`.
  98: - Cycle detection is also an observable signal:
  99:   - each recalculation that detects circularity in non-iterative mode emits at least one non-fatal diagnostic notification (for host/UI feedback parity with Excel warning behavior).
 100: 
 101: ### 3.8 Volatility and Invalidation Classes
 102: - Functions/UDFs are classified as:
 103:   - `Standard`,
 104:   - `Volatile`,
 105:   - `ExternallyInvalidated`.
 106: - Volatile refresh and externally-triggered refresh are separate pathways (`invalidate_volatile`, stream ticks, `invalidate_udf`).
 107: - Volatile formulas do not self-tick in the background; they update when recalculation/invalidation is explicitly triggered.
 108: 
 109: ### 3.9 External UDFs
 110: - External UDF registration/unregistration is in scope.
 111: - UDF volatility class participates in invalidation behavior.
 112: 
 113: ### 3.10 Engine Entities Beyond Cells/Names
 114: - Controls are engine-managed named-value entities with metadata.
 115: - Charts are engine-managed sink entities producing computed chart outputs.
 116: - Change tracking is engine-managed via opt-in journal/drain API.
 117: 
 118: ### 3.11 Formatting
 119: - Per-cell metadata formatting is in scope:
 120:   - decimals,
 121:   - bold/italic,
 122:   - foreground/background palette colors.
 123: - Formatting does not change formula semantics.
 124: 
 125: ### 3.12 API-Visible Invariants and Conformance
 126: - API-visible invariants are part of the normative contract for compatibility claims.
 127: - Initial invariant and case registry is defined in `docs/ENGINE_CONFORMANCE_TESTS.md`.
 128: - Property forms and temporal semantics are defined in `docs/ENGINE_FORMAL_PROPERTIES.md`.
 129: - Implementations claiming compatibility should report conformance outcomes against that registry.
 130: 
 131: ## 4. Non-goals (Round 0)
 132: - Multi-sheet workbook semantics.
 133: - OOXML fidelity and full Excel object model compatibility.
 134: - Collaboration/replication protocols.
 135: - VBA runtime hosting.
 136: - Full XLL/COM parity.
 137: 
 138: ## 5. References
 139: - `docs/ENGINE_REQUIREMENTS.md`
 140: - `docs/ENGINE_API.md`
 141: - `docs/ENGINE_CONFORMANCE_TESTS.md`
 142: - `docs/ENGINE_FORMAL_PROPERTIES.md`
 143: - `docs/SPEC_v0_INTEGRATION_APPENDIX.md`
### dnavisicalc-spec__ENGINE_REQUIREMENTS.md
   1: # Engine Requirements — DNA VisiCalc
   2: 
   3: Formal requirements for the core engine, aligned with `docs/SPEC_v0.md`.
   4: 
   5: Repository integration-only requirements that are not part of the core engine contract are moved to `docs/ENGINE_REQUIREMENTS_INTEGRATION_APPENDIX.md`.
   6: 
   7: ## 1. Scope
   8: - Single-sheet deterministic spreadsheet engine.
   9: - Externally-driven execution (no internal I/O, no autonomous timers/threads).
  10: - Includes structural rewrites, iterative cycle mode, volatility split, external UDF registration, controls/charts, and change tracking.
  11: 
  12: ## 2. Execution Model (REQ-EXEC)
  13: 
  14: ### REQ-EXEC-001: Externally Driven
  15: All state transitions occur inside caller-initiated API calls.
  16: 
  17: ### REQ-EXEC-002: Epoch State
  18: Engine tracks:
  19: - `committed_epoch`: increments on accepted mutations/invalidation events.
  20: - `stabilized_epoch`: latest epoch whose derived outputs are stabilized.
  21: - Per-value `value_epoch`.
  22: 
  23: ### REQ-EXEC-003: Recalc Modes
  24: - `Automatic`: mutation/invalidation paths may trigger immediate recalc.
  25: - `Manual`: mutation/invalidation marks dirty state; caller invokes recalc explicitly.
  26: - Explicit recalc API is valid in both modes (`force recalc` behavior in Automatic mode).
  27: 
  28: ### REQ-EXEC-004: Determinism
  29: For identical inputs and operation sequences, observable results are deterministic.
  30: 
  31: ## 3. Data Model and Addressing (REQ-DATA)
  32: 
  33: ### REQ-DATA-001: Bounds
  34: Default bounds are 63 columns x 254 rows (`A1..BK254`) with configurable bounds support.
  35: 
  36: ### REQ-DATA-002: Cell Inputs
  37: Cells support number, text, formula, and clear operations.
  38: 
  39: ### REQ-DATA-003: Name Inputs
  40: Names support number, text, formula, and clear operations with case-insensitive uppercase identity.
  41: 
  42: ### REQ-DATA-004: Reference Forms
  43: Formula parser and AST support:
  44: - relative refs (`A1`),
  45: - mixed refs (`$A1`, `A$1`),
  46: - absolute refs (`$A$1`),
  47: - ranges (`A1:B7`, `A1...B7`).
  48: 
  49: ### REQ-DATA-005: Name Validation
  50: Names must be valid identifiers and must not collide with built-in functions, boolean literals, or cell references.
  51: 
  52: ## 4. Recalculation Model (REQ-CALC)
  53: 
  54: ### REQ-CALC-001: Deterministic Recalc Outcomes
  55: For identical starting state and identical API-call sequence, recalculation results are deterministic (values, errors, epochs, and staleness visibility).
  56: 
  57: ### REQ-CALC-002: Recalc Completeness
  58: After recalculation stabilizes, all affected formulas/names reflect current inputs and invalidation events under the active recalc mode.
  59: 
  60: ### REQ-CALC-003: Internal Strategy Is Non-Normative
  61: Dependency graph/tree construction, scheduling order, and incremental-vs-full recomputation strategy are implementation details and not part of the required external contract.
  62: 
  63: ### REQ-CALC-004: Iterative Cycle Mode
  64: Engine exposes iterative cycle configuration (`enabled`, `max_iterations`, `convergence_tolerance`) and applies SCC-based iterative stabilization when enabled.
  65: When iteration is disabled, circular references use Excel-style non-iterative fallback semantics:
  66: - no dependency-status failure solely because a cycle exists,
  67: - circular reads use prior stabilized values when available, otherwise `0.0`.
  68: - circularity must still be surfaced via a non-fatal diagnostic notification channel.
  69: 
  70: ### REQ-CALC-005: Value Types
  71: Evaluation produces typed values including number/text/bool/blank/error.
  72: 
  73: ### REQ-CALC-006: Cell State Query
  74: Cell state query includes computed value, `value_epoch`, and stale visibility (`value_epoch < committed_epoch`).
  75: 
  76: ### REQ-CALC-007: Random Function Stability Profile
  77: `RAND` and `RANDARRAY` outputs:
  78: - stay within their declared bounds,
  79: - change only on explicit recalculation/invalidation events,
  80: - evolve via small deterministic perturbations between recalculations.
  81: 
  82: ### REQ-CALC-008: Normative v0 Function Set
  83: Required function set for v0 conformance (aligned with current Rust baseline):
  84: - aggregates: `SUM`, `MIN`, `MAX`, `AVERAGE`, `COUNT`
  85: - conditional/error handling: `IF`, `IFERROR`, `IFNA`, `NA`, `ERROR`
  86: - logical predicates: `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, `ISERROR`, `ISNA`, `ISBLANK`, `ISTEXT`, `ISNUMBER`, `ISLOGICAL`, `ERROR.TYPE`
  87: - core math/scientific: `ABS`, `INT`, `ROUND`, `SIGN`, `SQRT`, `EXP`, `LN`, `LOG10`, `SIN`, `COS`, `TAN`, `ATN`, `PI`
  88: - financial/lookup: `NPV`, `PV`, `FV`, `PMT`, `LOOKUP`
  89: - text: `CONCAT`, `LEN`
  90: - dynamic arrays and lambda family: `SEQUENCE`, `RANDARRAY`, `LET`, `LAMBDA`, `MAP`
  91: - reference helpers: `INDIRECT`, `OFFSET`, `ROW`, `COLUMN`
  92: - volatile/stream: `NOW`, `RAND`, `STREAM`
  93: 
  94: ### REQ-CALC-009: Staged Implementation Priority
  95: For staged non-Rust implementations, the following are critical-first:
  96: - `LET`, `LAMBDA`, `MAP`
  97: - `INDIRECT`, `OFFSET`
  98: - `SEQUENCE`, `RANDARRAY`
  99: - `STREAM`
 100: 
 101: Trig/scientific and financial/lookup functions may be sequenced later in staged runs, but they remain part of REQ-CALC-008 target parity.
 102: 
 103: ### REQ-CALC-010: STREAM Function Contract
 104: `STREAM` is a project-defined function (not inferred from Excel semantics):
 105: - signature: `STREAM(period_secs [, LAMBDA(counter)])`,
 106: - `period_secs` must be finite and strictly positive,
 107: - stream state is per cell formula location,
 108: - base stream value is an integer-like counter starting at `0`,
 109: - counters advance only via explicit `tick_streams(elapsed_secs)` invalidation flow,
 110: - engine does not autonomously tick streams in background.
 111: 
 112: If the optional lambda is provided, it is applied to the counter and participates in normal recalc/spill semantics.
 113: 
 114: ## 5. Dynamic Arrays and Spill (REQ-SPILL)
 115: 
 116: ### REQ-SPILL-001: Spill Semantics
 117: Array-valued formulas spill from an anchor into member cells with deterministic placement.
 118: 
 119: ### REQ-SPILL-002: Spill Blocking
 120: Blocked spill placement surfaces explicit spill failure behavior instead of silently overwriting existing inputs.
 121: 
 122: ### REQ-SPILL-003: Spill Queries
 123: Engine provides spill-anchor/range query surfaces for anchor/member lookup.
 124: 
 125: ### REQ-SPILL-004: Lambda/Map Dynamic Array Semantics
 126: `LAMBDA` and `MAP` are fully dynamic-array aware:
 127: - lambda parameters may bind scalar or array values,
 128: - `MAP` supports broadcast of input array shapes,
 129: - lambda returns may be scalar or array and must compose into deterministic spilled output tiling/broadcast,
 130: - resulting arrays participate in spill-reference semantics (`A1#`) like other array-producing formulas.
 131: 
 132: ## 6. Invalidation and Volatility (REQ-INV)
 133: 
 134: ### REQ-INV-001: Volatility Classes
 135: Built-ins/UDFs are treated as one of:
 136: - `Standard`,
 137: - `Volatile`,
 138: - `ExternallyInvalidated`.
 139: 
 140: ### REQ-INV-002: Volatile Presence Query
 141: `has_volatile_cells()` reports whether volatile formulas exist.
 142: 
 143: ### REQ-INV-003: External Presence Query
 144: `has_externally_invalidated_cells()` reports whether externally-invalidated formulas exist.
 145: 
 146: ### REQ-INV-004: Volatile Invalidation Path
 147: `invalidate_volatile()` marks volatile formulas dirty and propagates through normal recalc flow.
 148: Volatile formulas do not autonomously re-evaluate without an explicit recalc/invalidation trigger.
 149: 
 150: ### REQ-INV-005: Stream Tick Path
 151: `tick_streams(elapsed_secs)` advances stream counters and marks fired stream formulas dirty.
 152: - In automatic mode, recompute may happen immediately.
 153: - In manual mode, caller-triggered recalc remains required for stabilization.
 154: 
 155: ### REQ-INV-006: UDF Invalidation Path
 156: `invalidate_udf(name)` targets formulas/names that call the specified externally-invalidated UDF.
 157: 
 158: ## 7. Structural Mutation Path (REQ-STR)
 159: 
 160: ### REQ-STR-001: Supported Ops
 161: Engine provides:
 162: - `insert_row(at)`,
 163: - `delete_row(at)`,
 164: - `insert_col(at)`,
 165: - `delete_col(at)`.
 166: 
 167: ### REQ-STR-002: Deterministic Rewrite
 168: Structural ops rewrite affected formula and name references deterministically.
 169: 
 170: ### REQ-STR-003: Absolute/Mixed Ref Preservation
 171: Row/column anchoring flags are preserved through rewrites.
 172: Coordinate rewriting applies to all reference classes (`A1`, `$A1`, `A$1`, `$A$1`) under structural edits; `$` does not freeze coordinates against row/column insertion/deletion.
 173: 
 174: ### REQ-STR-004: Invalidated Reference Behavior
 175: References targeting removed coordinates are surfaced explicitly as invalid references.
 176: 
 177: ### REQ-STR-005: Bounds Validation
 178: Out-of-range structural positions are rejected without partial mutation.
 179: 
 180: ### REQ-STR-006: Valid-But-Rejected Structural Requests
 181: Structurally constrained requests may be rejected as valid commands that cannot execute.
 182: Rejected outcomes are deterministic atomic no-ops:
 183: - no partial mutation,
 184: - no `committed_epoch` increment,
 185: - explicit rejection reason via API diagnostics.
 186: 
 187: ### REQ-STR-007: Single-Reference Axis Rewrite Rules
 188: For row operations on a reference row coordinate `r`:
 189: - `insert_row(at)`:
 190:   - if `r >= at`, rewritten row is `r + 1`,
 191:   - else unchanged.
 192: - `delete_row(at)`:
 193:   - if `r == at`, reference is invalidated (`#REF!`),
 194:   - if `r > at`, rewritten row is `r - 1`,
 195:   - else unchanged.
 196: 
 197: For column operations on a reference column coordinate `c`:
 198: - `insert_col(at)`:
 199:   - if `c >= at`, rewritten column is `c + 1`,
 200:   - else unchanged.
 201: - `delete_col(at)`:
 202:   - if `c == at`, reference is invalidated (`#REF!`),
 203:   - if `c > at`, rewritten column is `c - 1`,
 204:   - else unchanged.
 205: 
 206: ### REQ-STR-008: Range and Name-Formula Rewrite Rules
 207: - Range endpoints are rewritten independently using REQ-STR-007.
 208: - If any endpoint is invalidated, the containing formula/name reference path surfaces explicit invalid-reference behavior (`#REF!`), not silent coercion.
 209: - If rewritten endpoints invert order, normalization to canonical range order is allowed.
 210: - Name formulas use the same rewrite rules as cell formulas.
 211: 
 212: ### REQ-STR-009: Spill-Reference Rewrite Rules
 213: - Spill anchors referenced via `A1#` are rewritten with the same single-reference rules (REQ-STR-007).
 214: - If the anchor is invalidated, spill-reference evaluation surfaces invalid-reference behavior (`#REF!`).
 215: - If structural edits intersect active spill boundaries that cannot be deterministically rewritten under current policy, the mutation is rejected (`valid-but-rejected`), not partially applied.
 216: 
 217: ### REQ-STR-010: Reject Kind Boundaries
 218: - `STRUCTURAL_CONSTRAINT`: valid request blocked by structural state constraints (for example non-rewritable active spill-boundary intersections).
 219: - `POLICY`: valid request blocked by host/engine policy gates independent of coordinate validity (for example policy-disabled structural edits).
 220: 
 221: ## 8. External UDFs (REQ-UDF)
 222: 
 223: ### REQ-UDF-001: Registration
 224: Engine supports register/unregister lookup by case-insensitive name identity.
 225: 
 226: ### REQ-UDF-002: Volatility Declaration
 227: UDF handlers can declare volatility class, defaulting to `Standard`.
 228: 
 229: ### REQ-UDF-003: Engine Integration
 230: UDF calls participate in normal dependency, recalculation, and invalidation flows.
 231: 
 232: ## 9. Engine Entities: Controls and Charts (REQ-ENT)
 233: 
 234: ### REQ-ENT-001: Controls
 235: Controls are engine-managed named-value entities with definition metadata and validated value mutation.
 236: 
 237: ### REQ-ENT-002: Charts
 238: Charts are engine-managed sink entities with deterministic computed chart outputs derived from source ranges.
 239: 
 240: ### REQ-ENT-003: Mutation APIs
 241: Engine supports create/remove/query/iterate surfaces for controls and charts.
 242: 
 243: ## 10. Change Tracking (REQ-DELTA)
 244: 
 245: ### REQ-DELTA-001: Opt-in Journal
 246: Engine supports enabling/disabling change tracking with drain semantics.
 247: 
 248: ### REQ-DELTA-002: Entry Shape
 249: Journal entries include typed entities (cell/name/chart/format/spill where applicable) and epoch tagging.
 250: 
 251: ### REQ-DELTA-003: Disable Semantics
 252: Disabling change tracking discards pending undrained entries.
 253: 
 254: ### REQ-DELTA-004: Circular-Reference Diagnostics
 255: When non-iterative recalculation detects circularity, the engine emits at least one diagnostic entry tagged to the producing epoch. This entry is non-fatal (recalc status remains success) and is intended for host/UI feedback.
 256: 
 257: ## 11. Formatting (REQ-FMT)
 258: 
 259: ### REQ-FMT-001: Metadata-only
 260: Formatting does not alter formula semantics.
 261: 
 262: ### REQ-FMT-002: Supported Fields
 263: - `decimals` (`None` or `0..9`)
 264: - `bold`
 265: - `italic`
 266: - `fg` palette color
 267: - `bg` palette color
 268: 
 269: ### REQ-FMT-003: Deterministic Enumeration
 270: Non-default format enumeration is deterministic.
 271: 
 272: ## 12. Enumeration Contract (REQ-BULK)
 273: 
 274: ### REQ-BULK-001: Deterministic Enumerators
 275: Engine exposes deterministic iterators for:
 276: - all non-empty cell inputs,
 277: - all names,
 278: - all non-default cell formats.
 279: 
 280: ## 13. Error Model (REQ-ERR)
 281: 
 282: ### REQ-ERR-001: Structured Engine Errors
 283: Mutating/querying APIs return structured errors for invalid address/name/parse/dependency/bounds and related contract violations.
 284: 
 285: ### REQ-ERR-002: Explicit Eval Errors
 286: Evaluation failures surface as explicit value-level errors and remain deterministic.
 287: 
 288: ### REQ-ERR-003: Outcome Classification
 289: Mutation APIs distinguish:
 290: - applied success,
 291: - valid-but-rejected outcomes (constraint/policy),
 292: - invalid/error outcomes.
 293: 
 294: ### REQ-ERR-004: Last-Status Diagnostics Retrieval
 295: Engine exposes handle-local last-status diagnostics for error and reject outcomes.
 296: Because these diagnostics are ephemeral across subsequent API calls, hosts must retrieve required details immediately after the triggering call.
 297: For reject outcomes, a single-call structured reject context surface (including reject kind and operation context) is required.
 298: 
 299: ## 14. API-Visible Invariant Set (REQ-INVSET)
 300: 
 301: ### REQ-INVSET-001: Invariant Registry
 302: The engine contract includes an API-visible invariant registry maintained in `docs/ENGINE_CONFORMANCE_TESTS.md`.
 303: 
 304: ### REQ-INVSET-002: Mandatory Initial Invariants
 305: Implementations claiming v0 compatibility must satisfy at least:
 306: - `INV-EPOCH-001`
 307: - `INV-EPOCH-002`
 308: - `INV-CELL-001`
 309: - `INV-DET-001`
 310: - `INV-STR-001`
 311: - `INV-CYCLE-001`
 312: 
 313: ### REQ-INVSET-003: Conformance Reportability
 314: Conformance outcomes are reportable at invariant/case granularity (`pass`/`fail`/`waived`) and are tied to a concrete engine build/version.
 315: 
 316: ### REQ-INVSET-004: Temporal Property Contract
 317: Temporal properties are part of the API-visible contract and use the forms defined in `docs/ENGINE_FORMAL_PROPERTIES.md`.
 318: Implementations claiming v0 compatibility must satisfy at least:
 319: - `TEMP-RECALC-001`
 320: - `TEMP-STREAM-001`
 321: - `TEMP-STREAM-002`
 322: - `TEMP-REJECT-001`
 323: - `TEMP-VOL-001`
 324: 
 325: ## 15. Non-goals for this Engine Contract
 326: - Multi-sheet workbook semantics.
 327: - OOXML read/write compatibility.
 328: - Collaboration replication protocol.
 329: - VBA runtime and macro execution host.
 330: - Full XLL/COM parity.

1: # Deep Research Synthesis: DAG Computation Theory for Spreadsheet Engines
   2: 
   3: ## Executive synthesis
   4: The strongest foundation for a spreadsheet-style DAG engine is not a single theory but a layered stack:
   5: 1. **Graph-theoretic skeleton** (topological order + SCC decomposition),
   6: 2. **Fixed-point semantics** for stabilization and cycle policy,
   7: 3. **Incremental maintenance discipline** (dirty/stale/necessary + dynamic dependency handling),
   8: 4. **Selective advanced incrementalization** (SAC/delta/differential) where cost justifies complexity.
   9: 
  10: This layered model aligns well with DNA Calc's existing architecture commitments (epochs, deterministic replay, profile-governed behavior) and gives clear proof/pack obligations.
  11: 
  12: ## Core architecture implications
  13: 
  14: ### 1) Separate semantic truth from scheduling mechanics
  15: - Semantic truth: fixed-point or acyclic evaluation result definition.
  16: - Scheduling mechanics: concrete algorithm (full rebuild, dynamic-topo, trace repair).
  17: 
  18: Why:
  19: - Enables swapping runtime algorithms without semantic drift.
  20: - Supports profile-based guarantees and deterministic mode.
  21: 
  22: ### 2) Make invalidation state a formal object
  23: Adopt explicit state model for each node/cell class:
  24: - `clean`, `stale`, `necessary`, `recomputed` (names can vary).
  25: 
  26: Why:
  27: - This is where most "hidden behavior" bugs occur.
  28: - SAC and Incremental literature show this is key to tractable debugging and analyzability.
  29: 
  30: ### 3) Treat dynamic dependencies as first-class
  31: Dynamic references (INDIRECT-like, external lookups) should not be bolted onto static DAG assumptions.
  32: 
  33: Use explicit lanes:
  34: - static dependencies (compile-time discoverable),
  35: - dynamic dependencies (evaluation-time observed, tokenized/provenance tracked).
  36: 
  37: ### 4) Reserve heavy math for high-leverage lanes
  38: Not every part needs full differential/timely machinery.
  39: 
  40: Recommended:
  41: - baseline: graph + invalidation + deterministic scheduling,
  42: - advanced: delta/differential model for external streaming and high-update hotspots.
  43: 
  44: ## Theoretical "best fit" shortlist
  45: 
  46: ### A. Mandatory baseline theories
  47: 1. Topological ordering and SCC decomposition.
  48: 2. Fixed-point reasoning for cycle/iteration semantics.
  49: 3. Deterministic replay and dependency soundness invariants.
  50: 
  51: ### B. High-value extension theories
  52: 1. Self-adjusting computation for dynamic incremental repair.
  53: 2. Dynamic cycle/topo maintenance for edit-heavy workloads.
  54: 3. Incremental lambda-calculus / change-theory for function-level optimization and formal proofs.
  55: 
  56: ### C. Strategic future theories
  57: 1. Timely/Differential model for external update semantics.
  58: 2. Semiring provenance for explainability and algebraic trace reasoning.
  59: 
  60: ## Risks if theory is ignored
  61: 1. Hidden non-determinism in parallel/invalidation handling.
  62: 2. Over-recompute and performance collapse under dynamic references.
  63: 3. Unprovable behavior drift between implementations.
  64: 4. Inability to explain conflicting outputs in conformance investigations.
  65: 
  66: ## Recommended next execution sequence
  67: 1. Formalize minimal DAG state transition model and invariants (clean/stale/necessary/recomputed).
  68: 2. Add explicit conformance requirements for dynamic dependency token lifecycle.
  69: 3. Build empirical comparison pack: full rebuild vs dynamic-topo maintenance.
  70: 4. Add targeted SAC-inspired prototype for one dynamic dependency lane.
  71: 5. Reassess whether differential/timely model is required for external-stream-heavy profiles.
  72: 
  73: ## Quality notes
  74: - Source set is strong on primary papers/specs and implementation references.
  75: - Some transfer conclusions are synthesis-level (inferred), not direct theorem statements.
  76: - Best immediate value is to convert this into explicit requirement/proof-pack rows, not to over-generalize architecture prematurely.

  30: ## Stable Decisions Captured
  31: ### DEC-CALC-007 Formatting-Sensitive Overlay
  32: - Default: `TEXT(value, format_text)` depends on explicit format string, not ambient cell style.

  36: ### DEC-CALC-008 Visibility Representation + Optional Visible-First
  37: - Model must include explicit visibility state (`visible_regions`, `visible_nodes`, `visibility_version`, priority policy).
  38: - Visibility can alter scheduling priority but not final semantics.
  39: - Deterministic queue key remains required (`priority_class`, topo order, stable node id).
  40: - Starvation prevention remains mandatory under visible-first policy.
  41: 
  42: ### DEC-CALC-009 FEC/F3E Seam Adoption Gate
  43: - Direction is conditional-go for transactional seam.
  44: - Required hardening themes:

  51: 1. Precise structural graph vs calc-time overlay lifecycle and publish boundary.
  52: 2. Overlay retention/eviction and epoch-safe garbage collection.
  53: 3. Spill invalidation algebra for prior/current spill regions.
  54: 4. Pure-calc fast-path guard conditions.

  61: Research framing and prior reconciliation converge on:
  62: - staged adoption (baseline deterministic topo/SCC first, dynamic-topo/SAC next, differential or timely only where stream semantics justify complexity),
  63: - obligation-driven synthesis (proof/conformance and empirical packs),
  64: - explicit separation of dependency discovery vs execution ordering artifacts,
  65: - trace-first evidence discipline for dynamic dependency behavior.
  66: 
  67: ## Program-Level Constraints Carried Forward
  68: 1. Deterministic replay artifacts are mandatory for conformance and regression work.

  70: 3. Epoch-tagged stale/pending visibility is user-facing contract behavior.

 820: Outcome model for structural functions:
 821: - `DVC_OK`: operation applied.

 830: Current v0 structural reject policy:
 831: - If a structural edit intersects an active spilled range boundary that cannot be deterministically rewritten under current policy, the operation returns `DVC_REJECT_STRUCTURAL_CONSTRAINT`.
 832: 
 833: Normative single-reference rewrite rules (applies to `A1`, `$A1`, `A$1`, `$A$1`):
 834: - Row axis (`r`) under row ops:
 835:   - `insert_row(at)`: if `r >= at`, rewrite to `r + 1`; else unchanged.
 836:   - `delete_row(at)`: if `r == at`, invalidate reference (`#REF!`); else if `r > at`, rewrite to `r - 1`; else unchanged.
 837: - Column axis (`c`) under column ops:
 838:   - `insert_col(at)`: if `c >= at`, rewrite to `c + 1`; else unchanged.
 839:   - `delete_col(at)`: if `c == at`, invalidate reference (`#REF!`); else if `c > at`, rewrite to `c - 1`; else unchanged.
 840: - `$` anchoring flags are preserved in rewritten formulas, but coordinates are still rewritten by structural ops.

 842: Normative range/spill/name rewrite rules:
 843: - Range endpoints are rewritten independently using the same axis rules above.
 844: - If any endpoint/reference is invalidated, the formula path surfaces explicit invalid-reference behavior (`#REF!`).

 846: - Spill references (`A1#`) rewrite the anchor using the same single-reference rules; invalidated anchors yield `#REF!`.

1320: ## 18. Thread Safety Contract
1321: 
1322: | Guarantee | Scope |
1323: |-----------|-------|
1324: | Multiple `DvcEngine` handles may be used concurrently on different threads | Global |
1325: | A single `DvcEngine` handle must not be accessed concurrently | Per-handle |
1326: | `dvc_api_version()` is safe to call from any thread at any time | Global |
1327: | `dvc_palette_color_name()` is safe to call from any thread at any time | Global |
1328: | Iterator handles inherit the threading contract of their parent engine | Per-handle |
1329: 
1330: No global mutable state exists. No global initialization function is required.
1331: 
1332: ## 19. String Encoding Contract
1333: 
1334: - All string parameters and outputs are **UTF-8** encoded.
1335: - All string lengths are in **bytes**, not characters or code points.
1336: - String parameters are **not** required to be null-terminated; length is always provided explicitly.
1337: - Output buffers follow the caller-provided buffer protocol: pass `NULL` buffer with non-NULL `out_len` to query required size.
1338: - The `out_len` value does **not** include a null terminator. If the caller wants a null-terminated string, they must allocate `out_len + 1` bytes and append the terminator themselves.
1339: 
1340: ## 20. Error Detail Contract
1341: 
1342: Each `DvcEngine` handle maintains internal last-status diagnostics:
1343: - `last_error_message` and `last_error_kind` for negative (`DVC_ERR_*`) outcomes.
1344: - `last_reject_kind` and `last_reject_context` for positive (`DVC_REJECT_*`) outcomes.
1345: - These diagnostics are handle-local (not thread-local) and are ephemeral.
1346: 
1347: Update rules:
1348: - On `DVC_OK`: implementations may clear/overwrite previously recorded diagnostics.
1349: - On `DVC_REJECT_*`: set reject diagnostics, clear error diagnostics.
1350: - On `DVC_ERR_*`: set error diagnostics, clear reject diagnostics.
1351: 
1352: Compatibility guidance:
1353: - Hosts should query needed `last_*` diagnostics immediately after the triggering call.
1354: - Hosts must not assume that calling one `dvc_last_*` accessor preserves another `dvc_last_*` slot for subsequent reads.
1355: - For reject outcomes, prefer `dvc_last_reject_context` as the primary machine-readable payload (`reject_kind`, operation kind/index, and optional cell/range context).
1356: 
1357: `dvc_last_error_message` provides human-readable detail; `dvc_last_error_kind`/`dvc_last_reject_kind`/`dvc_last_reject_context` provide machine-readable detail.

item.text:
**1. Findings**
1. The highest-risk gap is the missing normative publish boundary across `value`, `topology`, `spill`, and future `format/display` overlays. Foundation already requires immutable snapshots, epoch-tagged derived deltas, stale/pending visibility, no stale commit, and structural commit exclusivity, but the compact design notes still leave overlay lifecycle, publish ordering, and epoch-safe GC open. Without an atomic `CalcPublication(epoch)` contract, async recalc can expose cross-plane inconsistency. Sources: [A&R](C:/Work/DnaCalc/Foundation/prompts/runs/20260308-171858-core-engine-fec-f3e-deep-research-pack-01/inputs/source/foundation-core__ARCHITECTURE_AND_REQUIREMENTS.md#L6), [Formal](C:/Work/DnaCalc/Foundation/prompts/runs/20260308-171858-core-engine-fec-f3e-deep-research-pack-01/inputs/source/foundation-core__CORE_ENGINE_FORMAL_MODEL.md#L81), [Synthesis Context](C:/Work/DnaCalc/Foundation/prompts/runs/20260308-171858-core-engine-fec-f3e-deep-research-pack-01/inputs/source/synthesis-context__foundation_notes_and_design_draft_compact.md#L51), [Synthesis Context](C:/Work/DnaCalc/Foundation/prompts/runs/20260308-171858-core-engine-fec-f3e-deep-research-pack-01/inputs/source/synthesis-context__foundation_notes_and_design_draft_compact.md#L75)

2. The current FEC/F3E seam is strong on fence checks but not yet Foundation-ready for concurrency. It already has session/token/capability/snapshot validation, but the spec itself still lists threaded coordinator work and contention replay as open, while the current pathfinder API forbids concurrent use of one engine handle and relies on ephemeral handle-local reject state. Commit authority therefore has to move into a single publisher/coordinator layer. Sources: [FEC Spec](C:/Work/DnaCalc/Foundation/prompts/runs/20260308-171858-core-engine-fec-f3e-deep-research-pack-01/inputs/source/fec-f3e-current-spec__ENGINE_FEC_F3E_REDESIGN_SPEC.md#L46), [FEC Spec](C:/Work/DnaCalc/Foundation/prompts/runs/20260308-171858-core-engine-fec-f3e-deep-research-pack-01/inputs/source/fec-f3e-current-spec__ENGINE_FEC_F3E_REDESIGN_SPEC.md#L99), [FEC Evidence](C:/Work/DnaCalc/Foundation/prompts/runs/20260308-171858-core-engine-fec-f3e-deep-research-pack-01/inputs/source/fec-f3e-summary__implementation_and_runtime_evidence_compact.md#L42), [ENGINE_API](C:/Work/DnaCalc/Foundation/prompts/runs/20260308-171858-core-engine-fec-f3e-deep-research-pack-01/inputs/source/dnavisicalc-spec__ENGINE_API.md#L1320), [ENGINE_API](C:/Work/DnaCalc/Foundation/prompts/runs/20260308-171858-core-engine-fec-f3e-deep-research-pack-01/inputs/source/dnavisicalc-spec__ENGINE_API.md#L1342)

3. The layer split is directionally correct but still underspecified: structural refs and structural DAG as baseline, runtime overlay for dynamic refs/spills, and optional format/visibility overlay. The missing piece is one normative overlay contract that says what is persistent truth, what is derived cache, when overlay deltas are reusable, and when they force fallback. Sources: [Formal](C:/Work/DnaCalc/Foundation/prompts/runs/20260308-171858-core-engine-fec-f3e-deep-research-pack-01/inputs/source/foundation-core__CORE_ENGINE_FORMAL_MODEL.md#L186), [Formal](C:/Work/DnaCalc/Foundation/prompts/runs/20260308-171858-core-engine-fec-f3e-deep-research-pack-01/inputs/source/foundation-core__CORE_ENGINE_FORMAL_MODEL.md#L201), [DAG Synthesis](C:/Work/DnaCalc/Foundation/prompts/runs/20260308-171858-core-engine-fec-f3e-deep-research-pack-01/inputs/source/dag-research-synthesis__05_deep_research_synthesis.md#L30), [Synthesis Context](C:/Work/DnaCalc/Foundation/prompts/runs/20260308-171858-core-engine-fec-f3e-deep-research-pack-01/inputs/source/synthesis-context__foundation_notes_and_design_draft_compact.md#L20)

4. The current FEC delta split is a good base: `value_delta`, `shape_delta`, and `topology_delta`, with stable IDs and explicit spill events. What it still lacks for the long-term model is a generic typed overlay-token channel for format/display-observable dependencies, and the `prepare -> token/install -> session` handoff is clearer in evidence than in the top-level spec text. Sources: [FEC Spec](C:/Work/DnaCalc/Foundation/prompts/runs/20260308-171858-core-engine-fec-f3e-deep-research-pack-01/inputs/source/fec-f3e-current-spec__ENGINE_FEC_F3E_REDESIGN_SPEC.md#L25), [FEC Evidence](C:/Work/DnaCalc/Foundation/prompts/runs/20260308-171858-core-engine-fec-f3e-deep-research-pack-01/inputs/source/fec-f3e-summary__implementation_and_runtime_evidence_compact.md#L31), [FEC Evidence](C:/Work/DnaCalc/Foundation/prompts/runs/20260308-171858-core-engine-fec-f3e-deep-research-pack-01/inputs/source/fec-f3e-summary__implementation_and_runtime_evidence_compact.md#L111)

5. The policy boundary is correct: FEC emits evidence, the engine owns recalc policy. The pack consistently points to staged adoption: deterministic topo/SCC first, then dynamic-topo/SAC, then heavier differential/timely machinery only where stream-heavy profiles justify it. That argues against jumping straight to a self-adjusting core. Sources: [FEC Spec](C:/Work/DnaCalc/Foundation/prompts/runs/20260308-171858-core-engine-fec-f3e-deep-research-pack-01/inputs/source/fec-f3e-current-spec__ENGINE_FEC_F3E_REDESIGN_SPEC.md#L54), [DAG Synthesis](C:/Work/DnaCalc/Foundation/prompts/runs/20260308-171858-core-engine-fec-f3e-deep-research-pack-01/inputs/source/dag-research-synthesis__05_deep_research_synthesis.md#L40), [Synthesis Context](C:/Work/DnaCalc/Foundation/prompts/runs/20260308-171858-core-engine-fec-f3e-deep-research-pack-01/inputs/source/synthesis-context__foundation_notes_and_design_draft_compact.md#L62)

6. There is an explicit source-tension on cycle semantics. Foundation currently frames cycle mode as `CycleError` vs `Iterative`, but pathfinder v0 requires non-iterative prior-value/`0.0` carry-forward plus diagnostics. I would not silently pick one; the fix is to expand the profile enum to include `NonIterativeCarry`.
